text: {"version":1,"kind":"conversation","reading":"The user asks for a subjective recommendation on which player to build a team around, based on the prior points/rebounds/assists-per-game results, not a new data query.","measures":[],"groupBy":[],"display":[],"filters":[],"expectedShape":"scalar","unresolved":[],"provenance":{},"reply":"This is a judgment call rather than something the data alone decides, but looking at the 2017 per-game numbers (min. 20 games): Russell Westbrook stands out most for building around — he's averaging a near triple-double (29.0 pts / 10.1 reb / 10.0 ast), meaning he impacts scoring, rebounding, and playmaking at an elite level simultaneously, which is rare and gives a roster maximum flexibility. James Harden is the strongest alternative: he leads in scoring (30.1 ppg) and is also a top-tier playmaker (9.8 apg) with the most games played among the top three (96), showing durability. LeBron James offers the most balance and reliability (28.2/8.8/8.7 across a league-high 100 games), making him the safer, lower-variance choice if availability and consistency matter most. If the priority is a single do-everything hub to build an offense and defense around, Westbrook's all-around production edges it; if scoring plus efficient playmaking is the priority, Harden; if you want the most dependable, always-available anchor, LeBron."}
